author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Canonical record for A Maze of Death, PKD's novel. This single archive manifestation runs 104 pages.
page_summary:
A Maze of Death is the canonical works record for PKD's novel. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is A Maze of Death (1970). The archive copy runs 104 pages.

Researchers can use this entry to trace publication context, later commentary, and relationships to other works.

biography_events.event: PKD works out the invented theology of A Maze of Death — the Mentufacturer, the Intercessor, the Walker-on-Earth — the first system he treats as testable, not fiction.
biography_events.source: The Maze of Death Theology (Maze notes PDF)

biography_events.event: William Sarill becomes a long-term houseguest; conversations feed the theology that becomes A Maze of Death.
biography_events.source: William Sarill, Will the Real Ubik Please Stand Up?; A Maze of Death foreword

biography_events.event: Calling Ginger "Georgie" (memory leak from a past cycle).
Re-reading his own work and finding "impossible" correlations with 3-74.
Realizing "I am an illegal Christian" (The Thomas Persona).
Realizing the 1st Advent was level 1 breaking into level 2.
Recognizing the 3-eyed entities from the *Frolix 8* cover.
